convoLines.text: "Never mind the pantry run — we got it handled. Thanks anyway. My cut needs a second pair of hands. Could you clean it out for me? Please."
"It's getting worse, not better. If it festers I'm no good to anyone — can't haul, can't hunt, can't watch. Just clean it out and wrap it tight."
Move next to them, on the same side of the Haven door, to help.
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"I dreamed Caitlin was still here. Woke up angry at the dream. Stupid."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
You show them Wild Ginger — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to memory. "Good to know. Really good to know."
"Alright — I should get back to it."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
"This was good." They mean it.
"Has this changed you? Like, fundamentally?"
"…The old you got you here. The new you keeps you here. Both count."
"I used to be a truck driver who worried about being on time. Now I worry about being alive. Same worry, bigger font. So yes — and also no."
"...What's that supposed to mean?" Their voice goes careful.
"Still on how this changed you."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
They go very still. Not relaxed-still. Held-still.
A wall comes down, then — surprisingly — a door opens behind it. "I'm not from Denver. I'm from Brooklyn, New York. The truth felt small. The lie felt like someone worth keeping around." Quiet. Real.
"That again?" Tom sighs. "I confessed that already. I'm not confessing it twice for dramatic effect."
"You're really going to make me say it again?" Tom rubs their face. "Fine — but it's the same truth as last time."
"We went over this," Tom says, a little tired. "I already told you the truth about that."
They fill the quiet. "Anyway — where was I?"
"Okay. That's — I need a minute. A long minute."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"About that question — Any regrets? The real kind, not the small stuff."
Quiet. "Yeah. I think everyone's carrying one of those."
Their friendliness thins — still there, just held at arm's length.
"Still on your regrets."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Caitlin always took the burnt piece. Said someone had to. I take it now."
You show them Wild Ginger — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"I keep turning over the last thing Caitlin said to me. I can't tell if I'm remembering it right, and that's somehow the worst part."
"I should go. You know where to find me."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
If we don't write it down, it didn't happen. I'm writing it all down.
"Every name, every day, every meal. The boring stuff is the important stuff."
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Still on wanting to keep a record of everything."
They hear the warmth in it. They're not ready to let it in.
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
"Anyway — that's my cross to carry. What's on your mind?"
"Huh. I answered that once — back when the answer was simpler." "Caitlin is gone and the world just... continues. That's the part I can't stand."
You show them Dandelion — where it grows, how to tell it apart. A short laugh. "And I've been walking past it for weeks."
"Okay. We'll pick this up later."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"We never finished talking about what's been happening — we left it mid-thought, 7 days back. 'You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.'"
"Come see what I found. You won't believe it."
Tom shows you where they go to think. "Don't tell the others. Everyone needs one place."
"Same as always: we endure."
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"Still on what's been happening."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
"They're already drifting away. "Later."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"This was good." They mean it.

"We never finished talking about what's been happening — we left it mid-thought, 7 days back. 'You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.' We still owe wanting to keep a record of everything a proper ending, too."
"The plan is the plan until it isn't. Then we make a new one."
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
"Still on what's been happening."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
You show them Egusi Melon — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"Anyway — I should get back to it. Good talking, though."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"This was good." They mean it.
